newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end lower, some limit down.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end lower, some limit down.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures prices continued to retreat in a holiday shortened session and posted limit losses in late dealings as technicals and fundamental factors pointed lower, traders said.

October hogs closed down the 1.500 cent limit at 56.625 cents per lb with other months off 1.375 to 0.300 cents. May and July pork bellies held limit losses of 3.000 cents to close at 73.900 in May and 74.475 in July, a new contract low.
Carryover fund liquidation from last Friday's limit loss in October and sharp losses in pork bellies put pork futures in very weak technical territory, traders said.

"The (pork) market is obviously in technical troubled and we are not getting enough (good news) on the cash side of the market to stabilize the (futures) market and its just going to continue to feed on itself until the market is grossly overdone -- and we may be getting near that point," said Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
Levitt said the break in futures is making cash markets shaky, reinforcing the overall negative picture.

The larger than expected pace of slaughter also weighed on both pork pits. Hog numbers have been running above expectations from the last Hogs and Pigs report. This resulted in December hogs easing to their lowest level since September 5 and February bellies declining to their lowest level since May 31, traders said.
The heavy slaughter pace was especially negative to cash pork bellies, especially with futures falling as much as they have. The larger kills just added to the weak market tone, they added.
Both hogs and pork bellies closed early at noon CDT due to the Columbus Day holiday.
In hog options, commission houses were selling and buying December 54 puts early before the sharp break. Volititily was firm in both December and February, pit sources said.
